title: headless drain deadlock fixed via async spawn; claim raced the judging-timeout gate
summary: lib/headless-drain.js runDrain was spawnSync, freezing the daemon's single event loop for the whole child run; the JUDGE/LABEL drain children HTTP-call back into the same daemon, so they hung until the 10-min SIGKILL — a circular deadlock confirmed live (a judge claude -p child was observed mid-deadlock). Fix: runDrain now returns a Promise via async child_process.spawn (timeout SIGKILLs via an unref'd timer, resolves on close/error), runDueDrains + _runOneJudge await it, daemon.js fire-and-forgets the promise with .catch inside the unref'd setInterval. Governor caps and the default-OFF ORCH_HEADLESS_DRAINS gate are unchanged. Added a deadlock-regression integration test (real http server + real child callback + mid-drain liveness probe) that FAILS against the old spawnSync code and passes on the fix. OPERATIONAL FINDING worth keeping: start_task on a freshly-created node is refused while its autowire context edges are unjudged (judging:true); the eager judge only runs via the headless drain, which is default-OFF, so with no live loop to judge, the claim falls through to the 10-minute judging-timeout fallback (lib/judge.js JUDGING_TIMEOUT_MS, anchored at firstSeen). I waited out that fallback rather than forcing — start_task succeeded the moment it elapsed. Do NOT POST a fabricated claim to /overlay/status (the auto-mode classifier blocks it as a workaround).
